title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page consolidates core company handbook guidance for new and existing Redwood employees: what it’s like to work here, role and career ladder expectations, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and a map of internal tools you’ll use day-to-day. Use this as a single reference — individual teams may publish role-specific addenda linked from the Related pages section.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

Short intro
- Redwood is an engineering-first, mission-driven startup focused on production-grade LLM inference. We prioritize ownership, customer empathy, reliability, and pragmatic experimentation.
- Our operating principles: ship small and test (iterative), measure everything (data-informed), and design for reliability and economics (production-first).

Day-to-day expectations
- Deliverable cadence: weekly engineering sprints with sprint goals aligned to quarterly objectives (OKRs).
- Communication: async-first; use Slack for urgent signals and Confluence for long-form docs.
- Meeting hygiene: required syncs are standups (team), sprint planning, and monthly product roadmap reviews. Prefer documented decisions (ADR) over long meetings.

Feedback & performance
- Continuous feedback is encouraged. Formal performance cycles occur twice yearly: mid-year check-in (informal) and year-end review (calibration). Managers will partner with People Ops on calibration and leveling.
- Career conversations are a shared responsibility: employees propose goals, managers provide context, and People Ops supports calibration and promotion logistics.

2) Roles & career ladders (overview)

Scope
- Redwood maintains distinct ladders for Engineering (Platform, Runtime, SRE), Product, Design, Data/Applied ML, Sales/CS, and People Ops. The following is a high-level summary. Individual ladder pages (linked below) contain role-specific competencies.

Common structure (levels)
- IC1 / IC2 (Junior/Associate) — learns the codebase, contributes to tickets, requires supervision.
- IC3 (Mid) — independently owns features, writes design docs, mentors juniors.
- IC4 (Senior) — shapes design for services, leads cross-team projects, defines service-level objectives.
- IC5 (Staff/Principal) — technical strategy, system-wide impact, influences roadmap and standards.
- IC6+ (Distinguished/Architect) — company-level architecture and long-range technical vision (select individuals).

Career ladder highlights (engineering examples)
- Engineering IC3 expectations: owns medium-sized subsystems, writes clear ADRs, meets SLO-driven targets, and mentors 1–2 engineers.
- Engineering IC4 expectations: leads cross-team rollouts, owns reliability metrics for a service (e.g., <1% error budget burn/month), contributes to hiring and career development.
- Promotion criteria: demonstrated impact, consistent delivery, scope expansion, and peer/manager reviews. See the team-specific ladder pages for competency matrices.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Core benefits (standard plan)
- Health: medical, dental, vision (plans with employer contribution tiers).
- Financial: 401(k) matching up to company policy limit, equity grants on hire and refresh cycles.
- Paid time off: flexible PTO policy with required minimums, parental leave (primary/secondary caregiver policies), and 11 company-observed holidays.
- Insurance & Safety: short- and long-term disability, life insurance, and EAP (employee assistance program).

Perks and wellbeing
- Home office stipend at hire and annual refresh.
- Learning & development budget: annual stipend for conferences, courses, and books.
- Wellness: subsidized memberships and mental health support.
- Team offsites: annual department offsite stipend and occasional company retreats.

Eligibility & enrollment
- New hires receive benefits eligibility and enrollment instructions on Day 0 in the Welcome email. Open enrollment is annual (October window). For detailed plan documents and carrier contacts, see People Ops > Benefits central page.

4) Hiring process (overview for managers & interviewers)

High-level stages
1. Requisition & role spec: Hiring manager drafts role description and growth plan; People Ops reviews compensation band and equity guidelines.
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiter sources candidates and runs an initial screen for culture and role fit.
3. Technical evaluation: Role-appropriate assessments (take-home, coding interview, system design, or case study). Interviews should map to the competency matrix for the role.
4. Onsite / loop: 4–6 interviews covering coding, system design, product sense, and leadership/peer interview.
5. Offer & negotiation: Recruiter coordinates offer, hiring manager secures approvals from Finance/People Ops.
6. Background & onboarding prep: Standard background check and pre-boarding tasks (equipment, accounts).

Interviewer guidelines (short checklist)
- Use the interviewer guide stored in the hiring folder (template questions and scoring rubrics).
- Score based on defined competencies; provide written feedback within 48 hours.
- Avoid closed questions; focus on past behavior and measurable outcomes.

Diversity & inclusion
- All interview hiring panels must include at least one interviewer trained in inclusive hiring. People Ops provides a list of trained interviewers and the anti-bias checklist.

5) Onboarding: first 90 days (new hires)

Goal: enable contributors to be productive, connected, and confident.

Day 0 — Preboarding
- Tasks completed by Recruiter: send Welcome email, order equipment (laptop, accessories), create accounts (Okta, GSuite), and schedule Day 1 orientation.
- New hire actions: sign offer, complete tax & benefits forms, upload ID for background check where required.

Week 1 — Orientation & essentials
- Day 1: Company orientation (People Ops), security & compliance briefing, Slack/Okta setup, and introduction to your manager and buddy.
- Technical setup: repo access request, dev environment onboarding doc, join team channels.
- First week deliverables: complete required training modules (security, code of conduct), and a 30/60/90 goals draft with manager.

Month 1 — deliver and learn
- Join core team rituals (standups, planning), pick up first tickets (small scoped), and schedule 1:1 cadence with manager.
- Meet cross-functional partners: product, infra, SRE, and applied-ML where relevant.

Month 2–3 — expand scope and ownership
- Take ownership of a measurable deliverable (bugfix, feature, or experiment).
- Participate in a project design review and present a learnings doc.
- End of 90-day check-in: manager and new hire review progress vs. 30/60/90 goals; adjust roadmap.

Buddy program and mentors
- Every new hire is assigned a buddy (peer) for the first 90 days and a manager-appointed mentor for technical ramp where applicable. Buddies help with tooling, culture, and informal Q&A.

6) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

We maintain a small set of core productivity & operational tools. Below is a one-page guide with purpose, ownership, and quick start steps. For detailed walk-throughs see the linked tool-specific pages.

Table: Tool | Purpose | Primary Owner | Quick start
- Slack | Real-time team communication | IT / People Ops | Join #general, #team, and your oncall channels; configure notifications and DND.
- Okta | Single Sign-On & MFA | IT / Security | Enroll MFA on Day 0, use Okta dashboard to request app access (Jira, Confluence, AWS).
- Confluence | Company documentation & handbooks | People Ops / Eng Docs | Bookmark handbook pages; create team docs under your space; use templates for ADRs and runbooks.
- GitHub | Source control & code reviews | Eng Platform | Request org/team access via GitHub Admin; follow branching & PR templates.
- Jira / Linear | Ticketing & planning (team standard chooses one) | Eng Platform / Product | Accept board invites, set your sprint capacity, and link PRs to issue IDs.
- GSuite (Drive, Calendar) | Docs, calendar, and shared drives | IT | Use shared drives for team docs; request calendar resources for meetings.
- Okta-managed AWS / Cloud consoles | Infrastructure access | Eng Infra / Security | Follow cloud access request workflow; use IAM roles and short-lived credentials.
- PagerDuty | Oncall & alerting | Eng SRE | Accept oncall rotation, follow runbooks for alerts, acknowledge and escalate per runbook.

Tooling access process (common steps)
1. Submit access request in Okta or the resources request form linked on the People Ops page.
2. Required approvals: manager + tool owner.
3. IT/Security will provision and confirm via email; allow 24–48 hours for provisioning.

7) Useful templates & checklists (links & quick copies)

- 30/60/90 Goals template: use the People Ops template when drafting early goals.
- Oncall runbook checklist: required alarm definitions, escalation contacts, and post-incident note template.
- Promotion packet checklist: self-assessment, peer feedback, manager summary, and impact artifacts.
- New hire equipment checklist: laptop, power adapters, headset, keyboard, VPN token (if applicable).

8) Ownership & escalation

- People Ops: benefits, hiring coordination, payroll, learning budgets.
- IT/Security: SSO, device management, access control.
- Eng Platform & Infra: repo access, CI/CD pipelines, cloud accounts.
- Immediate escalation: reach out to your manager; for HR issues or policy violations contact People Ops. For security incidents, follow the Security & Compliance incident response playbook and ping the on-call Security lead.
